detail.longDescription: I'm trying to blit an image onto a rect and make it an interactive block, but I'm currently stuck on the part of blitting the image as it is not showing up in the output. class Sprite(Illust): def __init__(self, filename, filename_collision, x, y, width, height,): super().__init__(filename) #inherit methods and attributes from class illust self.filename_collision = pygame.image.load(filename_collision) self.width = width/2048 * 500 self.height = height/2048 * 500 self.rect = pygame.Rect(x, y, width, height) def display(self, filename, x, y, width, height, filename_collision): pygame.transform.smoothscale(filename, (width, height)) filename_rect = pygame.Rect(x, y, width, height) screen.blit(filename, filename_rect) pygame.display.update(rectangle = filename_rect) collide = False mouse_pos = pygame.mouse.get_pos() collide = (filename_rect).collidepoint(mouse_pos) if collide == True: screen.blit(filename_collision, filename_rect) pygame.display.update(rectangle = filename_rect) I am trying to make the image that will be stored as 'filename', to be displayed within a rect, and for it to change to a different image if the mouse is detected to be hovering over it. The problem is that it isn't even displaying. edit: here's the link to my previous question about illust: pygame OOP display and yes, the illust class and its current methods and attributes have all been run successfully
